title: GRE Format (Short Version): The One-Glance Map
summary: The current ~2-hour GRE — five sections, section-level adaptive Verbal & Quant, and how the scores work.

nodes.label: Analytical Writing
nodes.note: 1 'Analyze an Issue' essay · 30 min · always first

chunks.heading: Five sections, under two hours
chunks.body: Since September 2023 the GRE is **shorter — about 1 hour 58 minutes, five sections, no scheduled break and no unscored experimental section**. The **Analytical Writing essay is always first**; the two **Verbal** and two **Quantitative** sections follow in any order.
chunks.realExample: You write the Issue essay, then move through V and Q sections back-to-back. Compared with the old 3h45m GRE, there's no long break to reset — pacing and stamina planning change accordingly.
chunks.memoryHook: 1 essay + 2 Verbal + 2 Quant = 5 sections, ~2 hours. No break, no experimental.

chunks.heading: It's section-level adaptive
chunks.body: The GRE adapts **by section, not by question**. Your first Verbal section is average difficulty; **how you do on it sets the difficulty — and scoring ceiling — of your second Verbal section** (same for Quant). Within a section you can move back and forth freely.
chunks.realExample: Do well on Verbal section 1 and section 2 serves harder questions worth more — so the early section is high-leverage. You can flag and revisit questions inside a section, unlike a question-adaptive test.
chunks.memoryHook: Nail section 1 to unlock the harder, higher-scoring section 2. Early = leverage.

chunks.heading: How the scores work
chunks.body: You get three scores: **Verbal 130–170**, **Quantitative 130–170** (both in 1-point steps), and **Analytical Writing 0–6** (half-point steps). Programmes weight these differently — many grad programmes care most about the section that matches your field.
chunks.realExample: An engineering programme may focus on your Quant score; a humanities PhD on Verbal and Writing. Check your target programme's stated expectations rather than chasing a single 'good' total.
chunks.memoryHook: Two 130–170 scores + one 0–6. Your field decides which one matters most.

chunks.heading: Question counts and timing
chunks.body: **Verbal:** 27 questions across two sections (12 in ~18 min, then 15 in ~23 min). **Quant:** 27 questions across two sections (12 in ~21 min, then 15 in ~26 min). That's roughly **1.5 minutes per Verbal question and 1.75 per Quant** — tight but manageable.
chunks.realExample: If a single Quant question is eating two minutes, mark it, move on, and come back — leaving easy later questions unanswered to fight one hard one is the classic timing mistake.
chunks.memoryHook: ~1.5 min Verbal, ~1.75 min Quant. Never let one question sink the section.

recall.q: How long is the current GRE and how many sections?
recall.a: About 1 hour 58 minutes, with five sections and no scheduled break or unscored experimental section.
Analytical Writing — a single 'Analyze an Issue' essay (30 minutes).
Section-level adaptive: your performance on the first Verbal/Quant section sets the difficulty of the second.

recall.q: What are the three GRE score scales?
recall.a: Verbal 130–170, Quantitative 130–170, and Analytical Writing 0–6 (half-point increments).

recall.q: Why is the first Verbal or Quant section high-leverage?
recall.a: It determines the difficulty and scoring ceiling of your second section in that measure.
